### Project Name

Runkite

### Project Description

Runkite is a self-hosted control plane for AI agents, released under Apache-2.0. It separates operating an agent from implementing its model loop. A Go binary provides authentication, run admission and dispatch, connector access, human approval, spend accounting, audit and an embedded operations UI. Independent Python and TypeScript runners receive assignments over Runkite's gRPC Runner Protocol and execute agents using their frameworks' native APIs. Clients create Threads and Runs over Agent Protocol HTTP and consume SSE or WebSocket output.

Runkite also exposes configured agents as MCP tools and offers a decision API for applications that retain their own loop. That decision-only mode does not create managed runs or provide runtime cancellation or spend enforcement.

I began Runkite to address the operational work around agents across different SDKs without building another model-loop framework. The public repository dates from July 2026. The current published release is [v0.6.1](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/releases/tag/v0.6.1). SQLite and an in-process queue provide a local starting path; Postgres and Redis are the supported HA pair. This proposal seeks wider stewardship of the working implementation.

### Preferred Lifecycle Stage (if known)

Sandbox

### Alignment with AAIF Mission

Agent applications should be able to use open interfaces while choosing their SDK, model backend and deployment infrastructure independently. Runkite provides a working operational layer around those choices. Its strongest AAIF connection is MCP: an existing MCP client can call a configured Runkite agent as a tool, and managed agents can access external MCP servers through connector gates.

Sandbox would provide a place to develop neutral stewardship and independent maintenance before adoption patterns settle. The objective is a contributor and operator community around explicit interoperability and recovery contracts. Foundation affiliation is not being proposed as a substitute for evidence of independent use.

### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects

- **MCP:** The public `/mcp` endpoint implements Streamable HTTP using the official MCP Go SDK. Configured agents become tools whose invocation dispatches a managed run. Outbound MCP connectors apply Runkite's grants and approval gates. See the [implementation](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/blob/edf36c133955aeea3d9c28b353e64b0a64a3a3b4/internal/api/mcpserver.go) and [contract](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/blob/edf36c133955aeea3d9c28b353e64b0a64a3a3b4/docs/mcp-server.md).
- **MCP applications such as Goose:** A client pointed at Runkite's MCP endpoint is an integration opportunity. No tested Goose integration or Goose adoption is claimed in this proposal.
- **agentgateway and Agent Router:** AAIF already hosts gateways for agent, model and tool traffic. Runkite's proposed contribution is managed Thread/Run lifecycle, runner dispatch and recovery, and connector approvals around framework-owned loops. This proposal does not absorb or reimplement those gateways, and no tested integration with them is claimed.
- **Agent2Agent:** Runkite's internally named `a2a` API is subagent dispatch, not an implementation of the AAIF Agent2Agent protocol. This application does not claim that interoperability.

Runkite does not replace a client's model loop, an inference gateway or an external secret manager. It resolves configured secret references at connector session time. Native tools that bypass its connector or decision gates are outside its enforcement boundary.

### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption

Intended callers are platform teams operating agents from more than one SDK, developers who want a self-hosted managed-run backend for a web application, and MCP clients that need to invoke an agent with durable execution records. App-owned loops can separately request a policy decision before a tool call.

Working implementation evidence includes the published release, packaged runners, embedded Admin UI, public test workflows and documented deployment. A reproducible interoperability demonstration connects a native AI SDK runner to vLLM Semantic Router for model selection while Runkite retains managed-run lifecycle and connector authority:

- [Public reproduction patch and results](https://gist.github.com/sharanharsoor/84f4dbd4913106d06f8b8156fa8f47a9).
- [Accepted upstream documentation proposal, issue 5879](https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/issues/5879).
- [Published integration guide: One Conversation, Multiple Models: Runkite and vLLM Semantic Router](https://vllm-sr.ai/blog/runkite-ai-sdk-semantic-router/).
- [Merged upstream documentation PR 5883](https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/pull/5883).

The example is demonstration work, not a packaged integration in Runkite main. It is not evidence of production adoption or an endorsement. No independently verified production-adopter organizations are claimed here. The [Sandbox thesis](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/blob/216abde7885956dd02220848fb4b5ae7910a2c88/docs/foundation/aaif-sandbox-thesis.md) explains the pre-adoption case and how independent use will be evaluated.

### Governance Model

Runkite is currently founder-maintained. I, Sharan Harsoor, make final scope, merge and release decisions in a personal capacity. Ordinary changes use public issues and pull requests; vulnerabilities follow the private security-reporting process. There is no independent technical committee or multi-organization governance body today.

Public [governance](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/blob/216abde7885956dd02220848fb4b5ae7910a2c88/GOVERNANCE.md) and [maintainer documentation](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/blob/216abde7885956dd02220848fb4b5ae7910a2c88/MAINTAINERS.md) describe the current decision process, consent-based maintainer nominations and separately granted scoped permissions. LF charter and contribution agreements would be reviewed in the legal workstream before the Governing Board vote and executed after approval. No LF agreement has been executed or project assets transferred through this application.

### CI/CD & Release Workflow

Public GitHub Actions define Go, Python, TypeScript, Admin UI, adapter and offline managed-integration validation, OpenAPI checks, Helm rendering, actionlint, govulncheck and Trivy scans. Backend and framework checks have dedicated harnesses. These describe the validation process, not a guarantee that every deployment topology or live model provider has been tested.

Version tags trigger GoReleaser archives with checksums and OpenAPI artifacts, multiarchitecture GHCR builds, and runner package publication jobs for npm and PyPI. Releases are maintainer-driven rather than promised on a fixed schedule. The current GitHub release has Linux and macOS archives for amd64 and arm64.

- [CI](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/blob/edf36c133955aeea3d9c28b353e64b0a64a3a3b4/.github/workflows/ci.yml)
- [Release automation](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/blob/edf36c133955aeea3d9c28b353e64b0a64a3a3b4/.github/workflows/release.yml)
- [Release guide](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/blob/edf36c133955aeea3d9c28b353e64b0a64a3a3b4/docs/releasing.md)

### Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications

Contributors discuss contract changes through public issues and focused PRs. The [Runner Protocol](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/blob/edf36c133955aeea3d9c28b353e64b0a64a3a3b4/runner-protocol/PROTOCOL.md) is a working draft, version 0.1.0, maintained in the monorepo. Its [public mirror](https://github.com/getrunkite/runner-protocol) accepts discussion; patches land in the monorepo. HTTP changes include generated OpenAPI checks.

[CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/blob/edf36c133955aeea3d9c28b353e64b0a64a3a3b4/CONTRIBUTING.md) describes development, tests and Apache-2.0 inbound contribution terms. Contributors retain copyright. No industry-standard status is claimed for Runkite's Runner Protocol.

### Publicly Accessible Issue Tracker

https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/issues

GitHub issues and pull requests are the primary public project discussion channels. Security reports use the channels in SECURITY.md.

### External Project Dependencies

Principal dependencies include gRPC, Protocol Buffers, OpenTelemetry, the MCP Go SDK, Prometheus, pgx, SQLite, Redis, NATS, Kafka and MongoDB client libraries, LangChain/LangGraph, Vercel AI SDK and React. Optional Python profiles use Microsoft Agent Framework, OpenAI Agents SDK, Pydantic AI and Google ADK.

Terms include Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-style and ISC licenses. The declared set also includes MPL-2.0 components (`go-sql-driver/mysql`, `hashicorp/golang-lru/v2`) and Python Psycopg, whose current upstream metadata states LGPL-3.0-only. The MCP Go SDK retains its upstream MIT/Apache transition notice. Bundled fonts retain OFL-1.1 notices and Agent Protocol derived material retains MIT attribution. A Redis client license does not describe the Redis server license.

The [dependency scope and evidence](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/blob/216abde7885956dd02220848fb4b5ae7910a2c88/docs/foundation/dependency-scope.md) link manifests and notices, distinguish pinned from unpinned components, and list remaining review. I confirm that I am the sole founder and developer and that first-party development was undertaken in my personal capacity using personal resources. Third-party redistribution obligations and the full transitive and release-artifact inventory still need review in the legal workstream. This application does not certify a completed foundation IP-policy compliance audit.

### Maintainers & Contributors

Sharan Harsoor, [@sharanharsoor](https://github.com/sharanharsoor), founder and maintainer, participating in a personal capacity. Current contribution activity is visible in the [repository history](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/commits/main/). [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/blob/edf36c133955aeea3d9c28b353e64b0a64a3a3b4/.github/CODEOWNERS) names this account as the default owner. No additional active maintainer or organizational sponsorship is claimed. Growing independent contribution is an explicit goal of the proposal.

### Leadership Team & Decision Process

The current leadership is the sole maintainer named above. Decisions are made through public issue and PR discussion with maintainer final authority. Maintainer nominations consider review quality, understanding of runtime boundaries, collaboration and willingness to own an area, with explicit acceptance and a recorded decision. Titles would not automatically grant release, organization or credential access. This starting process would need to align with the LF-approved charter if admitted.

### Lifecycle Stage Evidence

Requested stage: Sandbox. The project has a working Apache-2.0 release and an actively committing maintainer. The [short thesis](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/blob/216abde7885956dd02220848fb4b5ae7910a2c88/docs/foundation/aaif-sandbox-thesis.md) provides intended users, the pre-adoption case, early integration interest and Growth graduation goals. The [community roadmap](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/blob/216abde7885956dd02220848fb4b5ae7910a2c88/ROADMAP.md) sets contribution, interoperability and independent deployment priorities.

The Growth adoption and organization-diversity bars are future targets, not present achievements. The roadmap anticipates a six-month Sandbox checkpoint and an application for Growth within twelve months if the evidence supports it, or a transparent reassessment otherwise.

### Security

[SECURITY.md](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/blob/edf36c133955aeea3d9c28b353e64b0a64a3a3b4/SECURITY.md) provides private reporting through GitHub advisories or the maintainer's personal email. Only the latest tagged release is actively supported. The project is solo-maintained and has no formal response SLA. CI includes vulnerability and image scanning; no OpenSSF Best Practices badge is claimed. Trust boundaries and unsupported configurations are public in [limitations](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/blob/edf36c133955aeea3d9c28b353e64b0a64a3a3b4/docs/limitations.md).

### Infrastructure Needs or Requests

Standard project infrastructure and onboarding guidance appropriate to Sandbox. Existing development and release automation is on GitHub. Infrastructure and account transitions would be scoped with LF staff during onboarding, rather than assuming a repository migration is required now. No funding, paid marketing, mentorship or foundation security-scanning commitment is requested at Sandbox stage.

### Additional Information

Apache-2.0 for current source and v0.6.1 onward. Previously published v0.6.0 and earlier BUSL-1.1 artifacts keep their original terms. See [LICENSE](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/blob/edf36c133955aeea3d9c28b353e64b0a64a3a3b4/LICENSE) and the [transition record](https://github.com/getrunkite/runkite/blob/edf36c133955aeea3d9c28b353e64b0a64a3a3b4/docs/internal/apache-2.0-transition.md). Dependencies and bundled third-party material retain their own terms.

This is a request for Sandbox review, not an announcement of acceptance. No project assets have been transferred and no LF agreement has been signed. The published Semantic Router integration guide and merged documentation PR provide early ecosystem integration evidence. They do not establish production adoption or an endorsement of Runkite.

Operational claims stay within Runkite's documented boundaries: cancellation is cooperative; connector governance does not cover bypassing native tools; MCP sessions currently need sticky routing across replicas. Existing package availability and checkout-only adapters are distinguished in the release docs.
